requirements.name: define-evaluation-model
requirements.text: jq is a small language with a large semantic core. Almost every filter is a **generator**: it takes one input and produces a stream of zero, one, or many outputs, and downstream filters run once per upstream output. Backtracking through that stream is not an optimisation, it is the evaluation model, and `reduce`, `foreach`, `limit`, `first`, `label`/`break`, and the `?//` destructuring alternative are all defined in terms of it. An implementation that treats a filter as a function returning one value will pass the early cases and then stall permanently. Decide the evaluation model before writing builtins.

requirements.name: run-conformance-harness
requirements.text: `sources/full_test.sh` is the single scoring entry point. It is supplied, not authored: it is staged verbatim into the build directory alongside the other imported assets, and `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score.

requirements.name: implement-lexer
requirements.text: **Lexer and parser.** Follow `sources/lexer.l` and `sources/parser.y` directly. Produce an AST. Precedence, `?` suffixes, string interpolation, and the `def` forms are all settled there. Reject invalid programs with exit `3`.

requirements.name: implement-parser-and-ast

requirements.name: implement-functions-and-bindings
requirements.text: **Functions, variables, and destructuring.** `def` with arity and closures, `as` bindings, object and array patterns, and the `?//` alternative operator.

requirements.name: implement-generator-core
requirements.text: **The generator core.** Evaluate a filter as something that yields a stream of values: `.`, literals, `|`, `,`, field access, iteration, arithmetic, comparison, and `empty`. Every later feature is expressed in terms of this. Get `[.[] | f]`, cartesian products over multi-output arguments, and short-circuiting right.

requirements.name: implement-operators-and-conditionals
requirements.text: **Control flow.** `if`/`then`/`elif`/`else`/`end`, `try`/`catch` and `?`, `//`, `reduce`, `foreach`, `label`/`break`, `limit`, `first`, `last`, `until`, `while`, `recurse`.

requirements.name: implement-json-and-structural-operations
requirements.text: Implement JSON values and structural jq operations.

requirements.name: implement-path-mutation
requirements.text: **Paths and assignment.** `path(f)`, `getpath`, `setpath`, `delpaths`, `del`, and then `=`, `|=`, `+=`, and friends. Assignment is defined over path expressions, so this cannot precede step 2.

requirements.name: reject-unmatched-exclusions
requirements.text: An entry that matches no case in the corpus is a hard error (exit 2), not a shrug — a silent no-op would quietly re-admit a case the kit cannot run if the corpus pin ever moved.

requirements.name: retain-module-grammar-cases
requirements.text: The module *grammar* cases — `module (.+1); 0`, `module []; 0`, `include "a" (.+1); 0`, `include "a" []; 0`, `include "\ "; 0`, `include "\(a)"; 0`, and `%::wat` — remain in the scored set: they are parse errors that a correct front end rejects without ever touching the filesystem.
